The second is their denial of the gathering, the resurrection, Paradise and Hellfire, and the totality of what the Quran's promises and threats contain, through various kinds of invalid interpretations. This is something we know that if any of it were mentioned in the time of the Messenger of Allah — peace be upon him — and the era of the Companions after him, they would have hastened to sever the neck [of the speaker] and would not have doubted that it was an explicit denial of Allah and His Messenger. So whoever denies Allah in His Oneness, does not believe the verses concerning monotheism, and does not believe in the Resurrection, the Raising, and the Gathering — how is he fit to assume the station of the Imamate and to have the ropes of Islam tied to him? This path is realized by the observer when he examines, then returns to their doctrines which we have mentioned in invalidating them. Thus, by the combination of the two considerations, what we have mentioned of the corruption of religion and the corruption of belief is established for him. How is one fit for the Imamate in whom is such a vice?

The second path is that we concede, for the sake of argument, by way of gratuitousness and acknowledgment to the one raising this question, that the leader of the Batinites is fit for the Imamate by purity of belief, soundness of religion, and the attainment of the remaining conditions. Then the path of preponderance is not closed off. For the Imamate we claim — the leaders of the age and the scholars of the time, nay, the masses of creation and the climes of the earth, from the farthest East to the farthest West, have unanimously agreed upon it, until obedience to him and submission to his command has encircled everyone upon the face of the earth — except the handful of the Batinites. Even if one gathered their entirety, their small and their great, their number would not reach the number of the people of a single town among the followers of the Abbasid Imamate. How then when they are compared to the people of a region, or the people of a clime, or all those upon the face of the earth who profess the Imamate? Does the fair-minded person doubt that the extremists among the Batinites, compared to the people of truth — if their small and great were gathered — would not reach a tenth of a tenth of the supporters of this victorious state and the followers of this rightful band? And if the Imamate is established by might (shawkah), and might is only strengthened by mutual support, assistance, and abundance in followers and partisans, and the mutual aid of the people of agreement and assembly — then this is the strongest path among the paths of preponderance. This is after we have granted them, by way of indulgence and gratuitousness, the soundness of their religion and the existence of the conditions of the Imamate in their leader.

If it is said: "No one denies the abundance of this band relative to them, but truth is not followed by abundance. For truth is hidden, and none grasp it except the few, while falsehood is manifest, and the majority hasten to submit to it. You have built preponderance upon the establishment of might through the abundance of supporters and partisans. This is only sound if the Imamate in its origin is contracted by the assembly of creation upon obedience — for that is not given preponderance at the time of permissibility and disagreement by abundance. But the matter is not so. Rather, the Imamate, according to the Batinites, is only contracted by designation (naṣṣ), and the designated one is rightful whether or not he is pledged allegiance, whether his pledgers are few or many. The one opposing him is invalid, whether his state aided him and his followers thereby became many, or did not aid him. So from what aspect is the inference by the abundance of followers sound?" — we say: The aspect of the indication of abundance is only made clear by understanding the source (māʾkhadh) of the Imamate. It has become clear that it is not derived from designation, as we estimated in the seventh chapter and alerted to the foolishness of one who claims the mass transmission (tawātur) of designation from each one of them upon his son. Rather, we have shown the ignorance of one who claims that concerning ʿAlī — may Allah be pleased with him. For if that were so, he would have adduced it and would not have been incapable of displaying it, nor would he have been content without it. For he it was who dragged armies and troops in the time of Muʿāwiyah until thousands of the heroes of Islam were killed in those battles, and he did not care about their killing. What then prevented him and his partisans from adducing the designation of the Messenger of Allah — peace be upon him? We have already shown that this is countered by the claim of the Bakriyya of designation upon Abū Bakr — may Allah be pleased with him — and the claim of the Rāwandiyya of designation upon al-ʿAbbās — may Allah be pleased with him. When the derivation of the Imamate from designation is invalidated, nothing remains except election (ikhtiyār) by the people of Islam, agreement upon advancement, and submission. At that point it becomes clear that whenever agreement occurs upon the installation of one — as they agreed at the beginning of the Abbasid Imamate — then whoever aspires to seek it for himself is a transgressor. For if they had differed at the beginning of the matter, preponderance by abundance would have been obligatory therein when numbers confronted and approximated each other. How then when all those upon whom the sun rises, rising and setting, have concurred — none opposing them except a counted faction and a paltry band to whom no heed is paid and no attention given, due to their anomalousness relative to the vast creation and the immense multitude who stand in contrast to them — "not a tenth of a tenth of their tenths, and they are but like a sip in the surging sea and the crashing wave"?

If it is said: "By what do you reject one who says: The Imamate has no source except designation or election. When election is invalidated, designation is established. The invalidity of election is indicated by the fact that it must either consider the consensus of all creation, or the consensus of all the people of loosing and binding from among creation in all regions of the earth, or the consensus of the people of the land in which the Imam resides, or be estimated by the consensus of ten, or five, or a specified number, or suffice with the pledge of a single person. It is invalid to consider the consensus of all creation in all regions of the earth, for that is not possible nor within the power of any of the Imams, nor was that prescribed in bygone eras for the past Imams. It is invalid to consider the consensus of all the people of loosing and binding in all regions of the earth, because that is either impossible or difficult with a difficulty requiring the waiting of a period that might exceed the lifespan of the Imam, leaving matters neglected during the waiting period. And because when the pledge was concluded for Abū Bakr — may Allah be pleased with him — they did not wait for the spread of news to the other regions, nor for the arrival of letters of pledge from the farthest climes. Rather, he occupied himself with the Imamate and plunged into undertaking the requirements of leadership, exercising authority in his commands and prohibitions over the elite and the common. When the condition of the consensus of all creation and all the people of loosing and binding is invalidated, then specification thereafter is arbitrary. For one who stipulates the agreement of the people of a town is not more entitled than one who suffices with the people of a quarter or a village, nor than one who does not stipulate the agreement of a region or clime. And one who does not stipulate the consensus of forty, or five, or four, or two is not more entitled than another regarding numbers. These estimations — those who hold them have gone to arbitrariness by mere caprice without any basis. Nothing remains except sufficing with the pledge of a single person. But persons are many and their conditions are conflicting, and no person is given preponderance over another except by infallibility. Thus the one designated as successor must be one, and that person must be infallible — and that is our belief. At this point, abundance avails nothing against those who oppose that single one distinguished by his particularity. So there is no refuge in the abundance to which you cling." — we say: Yes, the Imamate has no source except designation or election, and we say: whenever designation is invalidated, election is established. Their statement that election is invalid because it is impossible to consider all creation, nor to suffice with one, nor to arbitrarily estimate a specified number between one and all — this is ignorance of our doctrine which we choose and upon whose soundness we establish proof. What we choose is that a single person suffices to conclude the pledge of allegiance to the Imam, whenever that single one is obeyed, possessing an unassailable might (shawkah), and whenever he inclines to a side, the masses incline by reason of him, and none oppose him except those whose opposition is of no consequence. So the single followed, obeyed person characterized by this attribute — when he pledges, it suffices, because in his agreement the masses [are represented]. If this purpose is not attained except through two or three persons, then their agreement is necessary. The intent is not the specific pledgers themselves; rather, the purpose is the establishment of the Imam's might through followers and partisans. That is attained through every dominant, obeyed one. We say: When ʿUmar pledged to Abū Bakr — may Allah be pleased with them both — the Imamate was contracted for him by his pledge alone, but because hands followed in succession to the pledge due to his initiative. Had none but ʿUmar pledged him, and all creation remained opposed, or divided into an equivalent division in which no victor was distinguished from the vanquished, the Imamate would not have been contracted. For the condition of the commencement of contraction is the establishment of might and the turning of hearts toward partisanship, and the correspondence of inner and outer in the pledge. For the purpose for which we seek the Imam is the gathering of scattered opinions in the collision of contending passions. Conflicting wills and divergent, antagonistic appetites do not agree upon following a single opinion except when his might appears, his support is great, and his awe and reverence are rooted in souls. The pivot of all that is might, and might is not established except through the agreement of the majority of those whose consideration matters in every age.

When it is clear that this is the source of the Imamate, then there is no disputing that the noble direction which we support — Allah has turned the faces of all creation toward it and has instilled in their hearts love of it. For that reason, might has been established for it in the regions of the earth, such that if a transgressor appeared showing opposition in this noble court — even in the farthest China or the Maghrib — they would hasten to seize him and purify the face of the earth of him, seeking nearness to Allah — exalted is He.

Now it has become apparent to you how we ascended from this dark deep, and how we repelled what has perplexed all the masses of observers regarding the determination of the number of the people of election — for we did not determine a number for it, but sufficed with a single person who pledges, and we ruled the contraction of the Imamate upon his pledge — not due to his uniqueness in himself, but because souls are disposed to follow and pledge allegiance to one whom he has submitted to in obedience, and in whose following lies the establishment of the Imam's strength and might, and the turning of the hearts of creatures toward a single person, or two, or three, according to what the situation requires in every age. This is not a matter of choice attainable through human stratagem; rather, it is a divine provision (rizq ilāhī) that Allah grants to whom He wills. Thus, in appearance, we have referred the designation of the Imamate to the election of a single person, but in reality we have referred it to the election of Allah — exalted is He — and His installation. Except that the election of Allah appears subsequent to the following of a single person or persons. What validates the contract of the Imamate is the turning of the hearts of creation toward his obedience and submission to him in his command and prohibition. This is a grace and a gift from Allah — exalted is He. When He grants it to a servant among His servants and turns the faces of most of His creation toward love of him, that is from Allah — exalted is He — a kindness in His election of him for His vicegerency and His designation of him for following His commands in attending to His servants. That is a matter that all of humanity cannot contrive to attain.

So let the observer consider the rank of the two parties. When the Batinites ascribed to themselves that the installation of the Imam, according to them, is from Allah — exalted is He — while according to their opponents it is from the servants, then they could not explain the aspect of its attribution to Allah — exalted is He — except by claiming fabrication upon His Messenger in the designation of ʿAlī, and the claim of its persistence in his progeny, generation after generation, each successor upon his predecessor, and his designation of one of his sons after his death — various kinds of invalid claims. And when they attributed to us that we install the Imam by our caprice and choice, and they censured us for that, we disclosed to them ultimately that we advance none except whom Allah has advanced. For the Imamate, according to us, is contracted by might, might is established by the pledge, and the pledge is not attained except by Allah — exalted is He — turning hearts forcibly toward obedience and allegiance. This no human can accomplish. What indicates this to you is that if a vast creation whose number cannot be counted gathered to turn the faces of creation and their beliefs away from allegiance to the Abbasid Imamate generally, and from partisanship to the Mustazhirid state — may Allah aid it with permanence — particularly, they would exhaust their lives in stratagems and means, preparing causes and connections, and would attain in the end nothing but disappointment and deprivation.

This is the way of establishing proof that the true Imam is Abū al-ʿAbbās Aḥmad al-Mustazhir bi-Allah — may Allah guard his shadows — in this age. Nothing remains except the silencing of the objections of the deniers in their claim of the disruption of the conditions of the Imamate and the loss of the attributes of the Imams. And here we now show the face of truth therein in the form of question and answer.

For if a questioner says: "What you have mentioned of preponderance and the designation of this noble direction to one who deserves the Imamate is only completed if the existence of the conditions of the Imamate and the attributes of the Imams is shown. They have many conditions, and the Imamate is not contracted without its conditions. Rather, if disruption enters any of its conditions, its contraction is prevented. So detail the conditions and show their realization, that we may concede to you the establishment of the Imamate and invalidate the doctrine of those who say that this age and the near bygone ages were devoid of an Imam due to the absence of the conditions of the Imamate in the candidates for it." — the answer:

That which the scholars of Islam have counted among the attributes of the Imams and the conditions of the Imamate is encompassed by ten attributes: six of them are innate (khuluqiyya), not acquirable, and four of them are acquirable, or acquisition adds increase therein. As for the six innate ones, there is no doubt of their presence, and disputation over their existence is inconceivable.

The first is puberty (bulūgh): the Imamate is not contracted for a boy who has not reached puberty. The second is intellect (ʿaql): the Imamate is not contracted for a madman. For legal obligation (taklīf) is the pivot of the matter and its bond, and there is no obligation upon a boy or a madman. The third is freedom (ḥurriyya): the Imamate is not contracted for a slave. For the station of the Imamate requires the total occupation of times with the important matters of creation — how then is one devoted to it who is, as it were, lost with respect to himself, existing for a master who disposes of him under his direction and subjugation? How, when the condition of Qurayshi lineage includes this condition, since slavery is inconceivable in the lineage of Quraysh in any circumstance whatsoever? The fourth is masculinity (dhukūra): the Imamate is not contracted for a woman, even if she were characterized by all the traits of perfection and the attributes of independence. How is a woman a candidate for the station of the Imamate when she does not even hold the office of judgeship nor the office of testimony in most jurisdictions? The fifth is Qurayshi lineage (nasab Quraysh): it is indispensable, due to his saying — peace be upon him: "The Imams are from Quraysh." The consideration of this is derived from the revealed text (tawqīf) and from the consensus of the bygone eras that the Imamate is only in this lineage. For that reason, no non-Qurayshi ever undertook to seek the Imamate in any era, despite people's passion for domination and ascendancy and their expenditure of utmost effort and energy in rising to the station of eminence. For that reason, when the opponents in Egypt intended to seek this matter, they first claimed for themselves affiliation to this lineage, knowing that creation is in agreement upon their belief in the confinement of the Imamate to them. The sixth is the soundness of the senses of hearing and sight: for the blind and the deaf cannot manage their own affairs — how then would they undertake the responsibility of the world? For that reason, they were not deemed fit for the office of judgeship. Some authors added to this the condition of freedom from leprosy, vitiligo, chronic debility, amputation of limbs, and the rest of the repulsive, offensive defects. Some deniers rejected this, saying: There is no need for freedom from these diseases, for undertaking the affairs of creation and managing their interests does not require them, nor has any revealed text or act of worship come from the Lawgiver concerning them. It is not our purpose to show the sound of the two doctrines. Rather, the intent is that these six attributes are innate, not acquirable, and they are all present and attained — so no suspicion of obstinacy arises from them.

As for the four acquirable attributes — namely, might (najda), competence (kifāya), knowledge (ʿilm), and piety (waraʿ) — they have agreed upon their consideration. We now show the existence of the requisite measure for the soundness of the Imamate in Imam al-Mustazhir bi-Allah, Commander of the Believers — may Allah establish his state — and that his Imamate is in accordance with the Sacred Law, and that it is incumbent upon every mufti among the scholars of the age to issue a verdict with certainty of the obligation of obedience to him upon creation, the execution of his judicial rulings with truth, the validity of his appointment of governors and his investiture of judges, and the directing of the rights of Allah to him, that he may direct them to their disbursement channels and guide them to their proper loci and places. We speak upon these four attributes in order.

The discourse upon the first attribute — namely, might (najda): We say: The intent of the Imams by "might" is the appearance of power (shawkah), abundant preparedness, reinforcement with armies, the tying of banners and standards, the capability through the mutual support of partisans and followers to suppress the rebellious and tyrannical, to wage jihad against the unbelievers and the obstinate, to extinguish the blaze of sedition, and to cut off the sources of trials before their sparks flare and their harm spreads. This is the meaning of might, and it is attained for this sacred direction. For the might in our era, from the classes of creatures, is for the Turks — and Allah — exalted is He — has blessed them with allegiance to him and love of him, until they seek nearness to Allah through his victory and the suppression of the enemies of his state, and they hold as a religious duty the belief in his vicegerency, his Imamate, and the obligation of obedience to him, just as they hold as a religious duty the obligation of the commands of Allah and the affirmation of His messengers in their message. This is a might whose like has not been established for any other — how then is there disputation over his might?

If it is said: "How is his might attained through them, when we see them rushing to violate his commands and prohibitions and transgressing the limits prescribed for them therein? Might is only attained through one who oscillates under obedience according to capacity, and these, in their movements, oscillate only behind their appetites. When anger stirs in them, or appetite moves them, or rancor inflames their breasts, they do not care about following, and they know nothing but returning to what they were created upon of the nature of beasts. How then is might established through them?" — we say: This is a question of extreme feebleness. For the obedience stipulated upon creation for the establishment of the Imam's might does not exceed the obedience stipulated upon slaves and servants with respect to their masters, nor the obedience prescribed upon the legally accountable to Allah and His Messenger. The conditions of slaves in obeying their master and the conditions of servants in obeying their Lord are not free from division into compliance and violation. When the legally accountable were divided into the obedient and the disobedient, they did not thereby shed the skin of Islam, nor slip from its rope, as long as they believe that obedience to Allah is prescribed and that violation is forbidden and detested. Such is the state of seriousness in obedience to the master of the affair. For even if they violate one of the commands whose obedience is obligatory, they believe violation to be evil and compliance to be good. For that reason, you see them not changing their belief in allegiance, even if they were cut to pieces. There is no person capable of violating him in some matter who, when he reaches the noble threshold, does not strike the ground submissively, rub his cheek in the dust humbly, stand in the standing of the lowliest slaves at his door, and rise leaning on his feet upon hearing his address. If a rebel arose in a corner of the earth against this radiant state, there would be none among them who does not deem fighting for its sanctuary as jihad in the path of Allah, occupying the station of jihad against the unbelievers. What obedience in the world of Allah exceeds this obedience? And what might in the world confronts this might? Would that I knew — why do the Batinites not recall, when raising this question, what befell ʿAlī — may Allah be pleased with him — of the turbulence of circumstances, the falling behind of his partisans from him in battle, and their opposition to his judgment in most sayings and deeds — until no sermon of his sermons was free of complaint against them for turning away from him and being independent with their own opinions — until he would say: "No opinion for one who is not obeyed"? If his might was established through the following of the majority of his followers, despite the rising of those who rose against him, how then is might not established in our era, when the situation is as we have described?

If it is said: "ʿAlī — may Allah be pleased with him — undertook the matter himself, personally conducted the wars, appeared before creation, and did not veil himself from them" — we say: Who has stipulated in the Imamate the personal undertaking of matters and their conduct by oneself? Indeed, there is no harm upon him if he personally undertakes them. But if he is independent of enduring war personally through his soldiers and followers, it is permissible for him to confine himself to mere opinion and administration when consulted in matters near to him and his region, and to delegate to people of opinion whose insight is trusted in matters distant from him. This, in our era, is dispensed with — for Allah has subjugated the men of the world and their heroes to the allegiance and obedience of this presence, until they have dispersed throughout the regions of the world, as we witness and see. There is nothing beyond this might whose existence is stipulated for the soundness of the Imamate.

If it is said: "Why do you look to these and not look to the soldiers of the opponents, who are also reinforced with might in opposition to this might?" — we say: Whenever the abundance is on this side, the opposition of the opponents does not harm. Do you not see — why did the Batinite not look to the might of Muʿāwiyah and his preparedness, and his confrontation of ʿAlī with his soldiers and supporters? How then was it not stipulated for the soundness of the Imamate that the regions of the world be pure for him of the grit of opposition? Had this been stipulated in the Imamate, the Imamate would not have been contracted for anyone at all, from the beginning of the matter to our present time. It has thus become clear that the stipulated measure of this attribute is present, and more.

The discourse upon the second attribute — namely, competence (kifāya): Its meaning is the guidance to the right course of interests in the perplexing matters of affairs, and the discernment of the moderate path when evils conflict — like the intellect that distinguishes good from evil and by which the masses are judged fairly. The precious, aided intellect is one that knows the better of two goods and the worse of two evils. That is also in immediate matters, which are easy and near. What is obscure are the consequences of perilous matters, and none can undertake them except one aided by divine success (tawfīq) from Allah — exalted is He. We say: This attribute is attained, for its causes are abundant. For whenever it is attained from the innate intellect, free of imbecility and folly, the reaching of the consequences of matters by way of conjecture and intuition is built upon two pillars: The first is thought and administration, whose condition is acumen and intelligence. This is a trait in which the one aided in his Imamate and prescribed in his obedience — may Allah — is distinguished from his peers by an increase of penetration and decisiveness, until the greatest of the intelligent marvel in the perplexing incidents at his sound opinion, his piercing intellect, and his discernment of subtleties that elude the perception of the seasoned among the experienced. This is an innate attribute, and it is from Allah — a gift and a present.

The second pillar is illumination by the inspiration of people of insight and the seeking of the opinion of people of experience through the way of consultation (mushāwara). This is the trait that Allah commanded His Prophet with when He said: {«وشاورهم في الأمر»} — "And consult them in the matter." Then its condition is that the one seeking consultation be discerning between ranks, knowledgeable of positions, relying upon the opinion of one trusted for his cunning, competence, decisiveness, sharpness, compassion, and

chapters.title_en: Discourse on the Third Attribute, Which Is Scrupulous Piety (al-Waraʿ)
chapters.arabic_text: ### | القول في الصفة الثالثة وهي الورع
chapters.anchors:
- Root: و-ر-ع (w-r-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to be cautious, to abstain, to refrain" — specifically, the avoidance of anything doubtful or forbidden; also denotes the "side" or "slope" of a mountain (as a protective incline), implying a defensive posture.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, al-waraʿ is the virtue of abstaining from what is not clearly permissible (shubhāt), a higher station than mere ʿadl (justice) — it is the guard of the heart against worldly excess and the prerequisite for true certainty (yaqīn).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — physical withdrawal from a harmful thing; metaphorical (majāz) — the soul's retreat from moral and religious contamination, as in "a man of waraʿ" (rajul wariʿ), i.e., one who shields his religion.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The phrase "وهي الورع" (which is al-waraʿ) functions as an explanatory appositive to "الصفة الثالثة" (the third attribute), specifying the referent without a new syntactic break, maintaining the periodic flow of the enumeration.
chapters.translation: I say: Now for the discourse on the third attribute, which is scrupulous piety (al-waraʿ).

chapters.title_en: The Virtue of Piety and the Just Stewardship of the Imam's Wealth
chapters.arabic_text:
وهذه هي اعز الصفات واجلها واولاها بالرعايات واجدرها وهو وصف ذاتي لا
يمكن استعارته ولا الوصل إلى تحصيله من جهة الغير اما النجدة فتحصيلها من
الغير لا محالة والهداية وان اعتمدت على غزارة العقل ففوائدها يمكن فيها
الاستعارة بطريق المراجعة والاستشارة والعلم ايضا يمكنه تحصيله بالاستفتاء
واستطلاع رأى العلماء والورع هو الاساس والاصل وعليه يدور الامر كله ولا
يغني فيه ورع الغير وهو رأس المال ومصدر جملة الخصال ولو اختل هذا والعياذ
بالله لم يبق معتصم في تحقيق الامامة فالحمد لله الذي زين احوال الامام
الحق المنصور امامته بالورع والتقوى حتى اوفي فيه على الغية القصوى فتميز
بمتانة الدين وصفاء العقل واليقين في جماهير الخلفاء حتى ظهر
من أحواله منذ تجمل صدر الخلافة بجماله من إفاضة الخيرات والعطف على
الرعايا وذوى الحاجات وقطع العمارات التي كانت العادة جارية بالمواظبة
عليها كل ذلك اضرابا عن عمارة الدنيا واكبابا على ما ظهر من عمارة الدين
هذا مع ما ظهر من سيرته في خاصة حالته من لبس الثياب الخشنة واجتناب الترفه
والدعة والمواظبة على العبادات ومهاجرة الشهوات واللذات استحقارا لزخارف
الدنيا وتوقيا من ورطات الهوى والتفاتا الى حسن الماب  في العقبى فهو على
التحقيق الشاب الذي نشأ في عبادة الله هذا كله في عنفوان السن وغرة من
الشباب وبداية الامر ينبه العقلاء لما سينتهي اليه الحال اذا قارب سن
الكمال
إن الهلال اذا رايت نموه ايقنت أن سيصير بدرا كاملا والله تعالى يمده
باطول الاعمار وينشر اعلامه في اقاصي الديار
فان قال قائل كيف تجاسرتم على دعوى التقوى والورع ومن شرطه التجرد عن
الاموال حتى لاياخذ قيراطا الا من حله ولا يدعه الا في مظنة استحقاقه وقد
قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم اتقوا النار ولو بشق تمرة وليس يتم الورع
بالمواظبة على الفرائض واجتناب الموبقات والكبائر بل عماد هذا الامر العدل
واجتناب الظلم في طرفي الاعطاء والاخذ فان ادعيتم حصول هذا الشرط نفرت
القلوب عن التصديق وان اعترفتم باختلال الامر فيه انخرم ما ادعيتموه من
حصول الورع والتقوى قلنا هذا السؤال نكسر اولا سورته ثم ننبه على سر هو
منتهى الانصاف فنقول ان صدر الاعتراض عن باطني فلعله لو راجع صاحبه الذي
يواليه واستقرى ما شاهده من هذه الاحوال فيه افتضح في دعاويه وكان الحياء
خيرا له مما يورده ويبديه وان صدر السؤال عن احد علماء العصر الذين يعتقدون
خلو الزمان عن الامام لفقد شرطه
فيقال له هون على نفسك فان دعوى وجود هذا الشريط غير مستبعدة فان الاموال
المنصبة إلى الخزائن المعمورة اربعة اصناف الصنف الاول ارتفاع المستغلات
وهى ماخوذة من اموال موروثة له والصنف الثاني اموال الجزية وهي من اطيب ما
يؤخذ والصنف الثالث اموال التركات ولم يعهد منه قط الى الان الطمع في تركة
تعين لاستحقاقها وارث ومن لا وارث له فمنصبه بيت المال الصنف الرابع اموال
الخراج الماخوذة من ارض العراق ومذهب الشافعي وطوائف من العلماء أن أرض
العراق وقف وهي من عبادان الى الموصل طولا ومن القادسية الى حلوان عرضا
انما وقفهخا عمر رضى الله عنه على المسلمين ليكون جميع خراجها منصبا الى
بيت المال ومصالح المسلمين فهذه هي الاموال الماخوذة واخذها  جائز ويبقى
النظر في مصارفها وهي مع اختلاف جهاتها اربع جهات وفيها تنحصر مصالح
الاسلام والمسلمين الجهة الاولى المرتزقة من جند الاسلام اذ لابد من
كفايتهم واكثرهم في هذا العصر مكفيون بثروتهم واستظهارهم ومقتدرون على
كفاية غيرهم ومع ذلك فقد امدهم الراى الشريف النبوي في هذه الايام مدة مقام
العسكر بمدينة السلام باموال استفرغ فيها الخزائن وافاض عليهم من ضروب
التشريفات والانعام ما يخلد ذكره على مكر الايام والاعوام الجهة الثانية
علماء الدين وفقهاء المسلمين القائمون بعلوم الشريعة فانهم حراس الدين
بالدليل والبرهان كما ان الجنود حراسه بالسيف والسنان وما من واحد منهم الا
وهو مكفى من جهته برسم وادرار ومخصوص بانعام وايثار والمستحق لهم ايضا على
بيت المال قدر الكفاية وهو مبذول لكل من يتشبه باهل العلم فضلا عمن يتلحى
بتحقيقه الجهة الثالثة محاويج الخلق الذين قصرت بهم ضرورة الحال وطوارق
الزمان عن اكتساب قدر الكفاية وليس ينتهى اليه الخبر في حاجة الا سدها
ولا يرتفع اليه قصد ذي فاقة الا تداركها ومواظبته على الصدقات في نوب
متواليات في السر والعلانية كافية جميع الحاجات
الجهة الرابعة المصالح العامة من عمارة الرباطات والقناطر والمساجد
والمدارس فيصرف لا محالة الى هذه الجهة عند الحاجة قدر من بيت مال المسلمين
فلا ترى هذه المواضع في أيامه إلا معمورة وملحوظة بالتعاهد من القوام بها
والمتكفلين لها وهذا وجه الدخل والخرج
ونختم الكلام بما يقطع مادة الخصام وتبين فيه غاية الانصاف فنقول لا يظنن
ظان انا نشترط في الامامة العصمة فان العلماء اختلفوا في حصولها للانبياء
والاكثرون على انهم لم يعصموا من الصغائر ولو اعتبرت العصمة من كل زلة
لتعذرت الولايات وانعزلت القضاة وبطلت الامامة وكيف يحكم باشتراط التنقى من
كل معصية والاستمرار على سمت التقوى من غير عدول ومعلوم ان الجبلات متقاضية
للذات والطباع محرضة على نيل الشهوات والتكاليف يتضمنها من العناء ما
يتقاعد عن احتمالها الاقوياء ووساوس الشيطان وهواجس النفس مستحثة على حب
العاجلة واستحقار الاجلة والجبلة الانسانية بالسوء امارة والتقى في  ارجوحة
الهوى يغلب تارة ويعجز تارة والشيطان ليس يفتر عن الوساوس والزلات تكاد
تجرى على الانفاس فكيف يتخلص البشر عن اقتحام محظور والتورط في محظور ولذلك
قال الشافعي رضى الله عنه في شرط عدالة الشهادة لايعرف احد بمحض الطاعة حتى
لا يتضمخ بمعصية ولا أحد بمحض المعصية حتى لا يقدم على طاعة ولا ينفك احد
عن تخليط ولكن من غلبت الطاعات في حقه المعاصي وكانت تسووه سيئته وتسره
حسنته فهو مقبول الشهادة ولسنا نشترط في عدالة القضاء الا ما نشترطه في
الشهادة ولا نشترط في الامامة الا ما نشترطه
في القضاء وهذا ذكرناه اذا لج ملاح او الح ملح ولازم اللدد في تصوير امر
من الامور لا يوافق ظاهر الشرع وارادته الطعن في الامامة والقدح فيها عرف
ان ذلك غير قادح في اصل الامامة بحال من الاحوال
chapters.anchors:
- Root: و-ر-ع (w-r-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Abstinence, scrupulous avoidance of the unlawful; the root denotes a protective barrier and cautious withdrawal from transgression.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The theological virtue of waraʿ as the foundational moral state that safeguards the soul from sin, distinct from mere outward compliance.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage here—waraʿ as an intrinsic, non-transferable attribute; metaphorically, it is the "capital" (raʾs al-māl) of all virtues.
- Root: ن-ج-د (n-j-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Valor, courage, and high resolve; also elevated, rugged terrain.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A praiseworthy trait attainable through external aid, unlike waraʿ which is self-acquired.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in the sense of martial bravery; contrasted metaphorically with the inner, non-borrowable quality of piety.
- Root: ق-س-ط (q-s-ṭ) — though root ق is restricted, I note the term ʿadl (عدل) is used; anchor on ع-د-ل (ʿ-d-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Justice, equity, balancing scales; the mean between extremes.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The cardinal virtue of justice as the pillar of leadership and the criterion for lawful acquisition and disbursement.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal juridical sense—fairness in giving and taking; metaphorically, the axis upon which the entire Imamate turns.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa-l-istithnāʾ) — The text employs complex conditional clauses (e.g., "if this were corrupted...") and exceptive phrases (e.g., "no one is free from admixture") to structure the dialectical argument, requiring careful parsing of protasis and apodosis.
chapters.translation:
I say: This—namely, piety (waraʿ) and God-consciousness (taqwā)—is the most precious of attributes, the most august, the most deserving of observance, and the most fitting. It is an intrinsic description (waṣf dhātī) that cannot be borrowed, nor can one attain its acquisition through another. As for valor (najdah), its attainment from another is inevitable. And guidance (hidāyah), even if it relies upon the abundance of intellect, its benefits admit of borrowing through the path of consultation and counsel. Knowledge likewise can be acquired through seeking legal opinion (istiftāʾ) and surveying the views of the scholars. But piety is the foundation and the root; upon it the entire matter revolves, and the piety of another avails not in its stead. It is the capital stock and the source of the whole sum of virtues. Were this to be corrupted—God forbid—there would remain no refuge in the verification of the Imamate.

So praise be to God, who adorned the states of the true Imam—whose Imamate is victorious—with piety and God-consciousness, until he attained therein the utmost limit. Thus he was distinguished by the firmness of religion and the purity of intellect and certainty among the mass of caliphs, until there became manifest from his conditions—since the breast of the Caliphate was adorned with his beauty—the outpouring of good works, compassion toward the subjects and those in need, and the cessation of the constructions that had been the custom to maintain assiduously. All of this was a turning away from the building of this world and a devotion to what appeared of the building of religion. This, along with what appeared of his conduct in his private state: the wearing of coarse garments, the avoidance of luxury and ease, the perseverance in acts of worship, and the abandonment of passions and pleasures—deeming contemptible the vanities of this world, guarding against the pitfalls of caprice, and turning toward the excellence of the final return in the Hereafter. He is, in truth, the youth who grew up in the worship of God. All this in the prime of life, the flower of youth, and the beginning of affairs—alerting the intelligent to what the state shall culminate in when he approaches the age of perfection.

{«إِنَّ الْهِلَالَ إِذَا رَأَيْتَ نُمُوَّهُ أَيْقَنْتَ أَنَّ سَيَصِيرُ بَدْرًا كَامِلًا»} — "When you see the crescent's growth, you are certain it shall become a full moon." And God Most High extends him with the longest of lifespans and spreads his banners in the farthest of lands.

If a questioner says: "How have you dared to claim piety and God-consciousness, whose condition is the renunciation of wealth, such that one takes not a single qīrāṭ except from its lawful source, nor leaves it except where its entitlement is presumed? For the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: {«اتَّقُوا النَّارَ وَلَوْ بِشِقِّ تَمْرَةٍ»} — 'Guard against the Fire even with half a date.' And piety is not perfected by perseverance in the obligatory duties and avoidance of grave sins and enormities; rather, the pillar of this matter is justice and the avoidance of injustice in both giving and taking. If you claim the attainment of this condition, hearts recoil from belief; and if you admit its corruption, then what you have claimed of the attainment of piety and God-consciousness is breached."

We say: This question—first we break its force, then we point to a secret that is the utmost of fairness. We say: if the objection issues from a Bāṭinī, perhaps were he to consult his companion whom he follows and survey what he has witnessed of these states in him, he would be exposed in his claims, and shame would be better for him than what he advances and displays. And if the question issues from one of the scholars of the age who believe the time is devoid of an Imam for lack of his condition, then it is said to him: "Ease yourself, for the claim of the existence of this condition is not improbable."

For the wealth flowing into the flourishing treasuries is of four kinds. The first kind: the revenues of estates (mustaghallāt), which are taken from inherited properties belonging to him. The second kind: the funds of the poll-tax (jizyah), which are among the most wholesome of what is taken. The third kind: the funds of inheritances (tarakāt)—and never has there been witnessed from him, to this day, any covetousness toward an inheritance designated for an entitled heir; and he who has no heir, his portion goes to the treasury of the Muslims (bayt al-māl). The fourth kind: the funds of the land-tax (kharāj) taken from the lands of Iraq. The doctrine of al-Shāfiʿī, may God be pleased with him, and groups of scholars is that the land of Iraq is an endowment (waqf)—from ʿAbbādān to al-Mawṣil in length, and from al-Qādisiyyah to Ḥulwān in breadth—endowed by ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, upon the Muslims, so that all its land-tax flows to the treasury of the Muslims and the interests of the Muslims.

These, then, are the funds taken, and their taking is permissible. What remains is the consideration of their expenditures, which, despite the diversity of their channels, are of four directions, and in them are encompassed the interests of Islam and the Muslims.

The first direction: the salaried soldiers of Islam (murtaziqah), for their sufficiency is indispensable. Most of them in this age are rendered self-sufficient by their own wealth and reinforcement, and are capable of providing for others. Nevertheless, the noble prophetic judgment has, in these days, supplied them—during the army's sojourn in the City of Peace (Baghdad)—with funds that exhausted the treasuries, and lavished upon them varieties of honors and benefactions whose remembrance shall endure through the vicissitudes of days and years.

The second direction: the scholars of religion and the jurists of the Muslims who uphold the sciences of the Sacred Law, for they are the guardians of religion by proof and demonstration, just as the soldiers are its guardians by sword and spear. There is not one of them but is provided for from his quarter with a stipend and regular allowance, and distinguished with benefaction and preference. What is due to them from the treasury of the Muslims is the amount of sufficiency, and it is disbursed to every one who emulates the people of knowledge, let alone him who is invested in its verification.

The third direction: the needy of creation whose exigencies of circumstance and calamities of time have prevented them from earning the measure of sufficiency. No report of a need reaches him but he fills it, and no intent of a destitute person rises to him but he overtakes it. His perseverance in alms-giving in successive turns, in secret and in public, suffices for all needs.

The fourth direction: the public interests—the construction of hospices (ribāṭāt), bridges, mosques, and schools. To this direction is necessarily expended, at the time of need, a portion from the treasury of the Muslims. Thus you see these places in his days only as flourishing, and attended to by the care of those who maintain them and undertake them. This is the aspect of income and expenditure.

And we conclude the discourse with what severs the material of contention and manifests therein the utmost fairness. We say: Let no one suppose that we stipulate in the Imamate infallibility (ʿiṣmah). For the scholars have differed concerning its attainment for the prophets, and the majority hold that they were not protected from minor sins (ṣaghāʾir). Were infallibility from every slip to be considered, then governorships would become impossible, judges would be removed, and the Imamate would be nullified. How can one judge by the stipulation of purity from every disobedience and the persistence upon the path of piety without deviation? It is known that natural constitutions (jibillāt) demand pleasures, and temperaments incite toward the attainment of passions. The obligations (takālīf) entail a burden that even the strong are incapable of bearing. The whisperings of Satan and the promptings of the soul urge toward love of the immediate and contempt for the deferred. The human constitution is commanding toward evil—{«إِنَّ النَّفْسَ لَأَمَّارَةٌ بِالسُّوءِ»}—and piety is in the swing of caprice: it prevails at times and fails at times. Satan does not slacken in his whisperings, and slips almost flow with every breath. How then can a human being escape the assault of a prohibited thing and the plunge into a forbidden one?

For this reason, al-Shāfiʿī, may God be pleased with him, said concerning the condition of a witness's probity (ʿadālah): "No one is known by pure obedience such that he is not sullied with a sin, nor by pure disobedience such that he does not advance upon an act of obedience. No one is free from admixture (takhlīṭ). But he whose acts of obedience prevail in his case over his acts of disobedience, and whose evil deed grieves him and whose good deed delights him—his testimony is accepted." And we do not stipulate in the probity of the judiciary (qaḍāʾ) anything beyond what we stipulate in testimony, nor do we stipulate in the Imamate anything beyond what we stipulate in the judiciary.

This we have mentioned so that if a disputant persists, or an obstinate one presses, and clings to contentiousness in depicting a matter that does not accord with the apparent sense of the Sacred Law, intending thereby to impugn the Imamate and cast aspersion upon it, it becomes known that this is not, in any state of affairs, a defect in the foundation of the Imamate.

chapters.title_en: Discourse on the Fourth Attribute — Knowledge (al-ʿIlm)
chapters.arabic_text: ### | القول في الصفة الرابعة وهي العلم
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-L-M)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning — knowing, perceiving, or being cognizant of something as it truly is; also a mark or trace by which something is recognized.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, ʿilm is the firm, stable comprehension of an object’s reality (ḥaqīqah), distinct from mere opinion (ẓann) or imitation (taqlīd); it is an attribute of God and a perfection of the rational soul.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — direct, certain knowledge; metaphorical (majāz) — knowledge as a "sign" (ʿalamah) pointing to its object, or as a faculty of discernment.
- Sībawayh Rule: Nominal Predication (al-Isnād al-Ismī) — The phrase "al-ṣifah al-rābiʿah wa-hiya al-ʿilm" employs a nominal sentence with an explicit subject (al-ṣifah) and a pronominal predicate (hiya), establishing a definitive identification of the attribute under discussion.
chapters.translation: I say: Now we proceed to the discourse on the fourth attribute, which is knowledge (al-ʿilm). Know that the Bāṭinites claim for their Imām a knowledge that is divinely inspired (ladunī) and infallibly preserved, yet they render it inaccessible to rational inquiry and immune to verification. But we shall expose the vacuity of this claim by examining what they affirm concerning the nature of this knowledge, its source, and its object — for if their doctrine collapses at any of these points, their entire edifice falls.

chapters.title_en: The Condition of Ijtihad in the Imamate and the Validity of the Current Imamate
chapters.arabic_text:
فإن قال قائل اتفق راي العلماء على أن الامامة لا تنعقد الا لمن نال رتبة
الاجتهاد والفتوى في علوم الشرع ولا يمكنكم دعوى وجود هذه الشريطة ولو
ادعيتم أن ذلك لا يشترط كان انسلالا عن وفاق العلماء قاطبة فما رأيكم في
هذه الصفة
قلنا لو ذهب ذاهب إلى أن بلوغ درجة الاجتهاد لا يشترط في الامامة لم يكن
في كلامه الا الاعزاب عن العلماء الماضين والا فليس فيه ما يخالف مقتضى
الدليل وسياق النظر فان الشروط التي تدعى للامامة شرعا لابد من دليل يدل
عليها والدليل اما نص من صاحب الشرع واما النظر في المصلحة التي طلبت
الامامة لها ولم يرد النص من شرائط الامامة في شيء الا في النسب اذ قال أن
الائمة من قريش فاما ما عداه فانما اخذ من الضرورة والحاجة الماسة في مقصود
الامامة اليها فهذا كما شرطنا العقل والحرية وسلامة الحواس والهداية
والنجدة والورع فان هذه الامور لو قدر عدمها لم ينتظم امر الامامة بحال من
الاحوال وليست رتبة الاجتهاد مما لا بد منه في الامامة ضرورة بل الورع
الداعي الى مراجعة  اهل العلم فيه كاف فاذا كان المقصود ترتيب الامامة على
وفق الشرع فاى فرق بين ان يعرف حكم الشرع بنظره او يعرفه باتباع افضل اهل
زمانه واذا جاز للمجتهد ان يعول على قول واحد ويروى له حديثا فيحكم به
إماما كان او قاضيا فما المانع من ان يحكم بما يتفق عليه العلماء في كل
واقعة وان اختلف
فيتبع فيه قوله الافضل الاعلم ولم لا يكون مكملا بافضل اهل الزمان مقصود
العلم كما كمل باقوى اهل الزمان مقصود الشوكة وبادهى اهل الزمان وأكفاهم
رأيا ونظرا مقصود الكفاية فلا تزال دولته محفوفة بملك من الملوك قوى يمده
بشوكته وكاف من كفاة الزمان يتصدى لوزارته فيمده برايه وهدايته وعالم مقدم
في العلوم يفيض ما يلوح من قضايا الشرع في كل واقعة إلى حضرته هذا لو قال
به قائل لكان مستمدا من قواطع الادلة والبراهين التى يجوز استعمالها في
مظان القطع واليقين فكيف في مواقع الظن والتخمين واكثر مسائل الامامة
واحكامها مسائل فقهية ظنية يحكم فيها بموجب الراى الاغلب وما ذكرته مسلك
واضح فيه ولكنى لا اوثر الاعزاب عن الماضين ولا الانحراف عن جادة الائمة
المنقرضين فان الانفراد بالراى والانسلال عن موافقة الجماهير لا ينفك عن
اثارة نفرة القلوب لكني استميح مسلكا مقتبسا من كلام الائمة المذكورين
واقول اختلف الناس في ان اهل الاختيار لو عقدوا عقد البيعة للمفضول واعرضوا
عن الافضل هل تنعقد الامامة مع الاتفاق على ان تقديم الافضل عند القدرة
واجب متعين ثم ذهب الاكثرون إلى انها اذا عقدت للمفضول مع حضور الافضل
انعقدت ولم يجز خلعه لسبب الافضل وانا من هذا انشئ واقول أن رددناها في
مبدا التولية بين مجتهد في علوم الشرع وبين متقاصر عنها فيتعين تقديم
المجتهد لان اتباع الناظر علم نفسه له مزية رتبة على اتباع علم غيره
بالتقليد والمزايا لا سبيل إلى إهمالها مع القدرة على مراعاتها أما إذا
انعقدت الإمامة بالبيعة أوتولية العهد لمنفك عن رتبة الاجتهاد وقامت له
شوكة واذعنت له الرقاب ومالت اليه  القلوب فان خلا الزمان عن قرشي مجتهد
يستجمع
جميع الشروط وجب الاستمرار على الامامة المعقودة ان قامت له الشوكة وهذا
حكم زماننا وان قدر ضربا للمثل حضور قرشي مجتهد مستجمع للورع والكفاية
وجميع شرائط الامامة واحتاج المسلمون في خلع الاول إلى تعرض لاثارة فتن
واضطراب امور لم يجز لهم خلعه والاستبدال به بل تجب عليهم الطاعة له والحكم
بنفوذ ولايته وصحة إمامته لأنا نعلم بأن العلم مزية روعيت في الإمامة
تحسينا للأمر وتحصيلا لمزيد المصلحة في الاستقلال بالنظر والاستغناء عن
التقليد وان الثمرة المطلوبة من الإمامة تطفئة الفتن الثائرة في تفرق
الآراء المتنافرة فكيف يستجيز العاقل تحريك الفتنة وتشويش نظام الأمور
وتفويت أصل المصلحة في الحال تشوفا إلى مزيد دقيقة في الفرق بين النظر
والتقليد وعند هذا ينبغي أن يقيس الانسان ما ينال الخلق بسبب عدول الإمام
عن النظر إلى تقليد الأئمة بما ينالهم لو تعرضوا لخلعه واستبداله أو حكموا
إمامته غير منعقدة وإذا أحسن إيراد هذه المقالة علم أن التفاوت بين اتباع
الشرع نظرا واتباعه تقليدا قريب هين وانه لا يجوز أن تخرم بسببه قواعد
الإمامة وهذا تقدير تسامحنا به من وجهين أحدهما تقدير قرشي مجتهد مستجمع
الصفات متصد لطلب الإمامة وهذا لا وجود له في عصرنا والثاني تقدير
اقتدارالخلق على الاستبدال بالإمام والتصرف فيه بالخلع والانتقال وهذا محال
في زماننا إذ لو أجمع أهل الدهر وتألبوا على أن يصرفوا الوجوه والقلوب عن
الحضرة المقدسة المستظهرية لم يجدوا اليها سبيلا فيتعين على كافة علماء
العصر الفتوى بصحة هذه الإمامة وانعقادها بالشرع ولكن بعد هذا شرطان أحدهما
أن لا يمضي كل قضية مشكلة إلا بعد استنتاج قرائح العلماء والاستظهار بهم
وأن يختار لتقليده عند التباس الأمر واختلاف الكلمة أفضل أهل الزمان
واغزرهم علما وقلما تنفك مدينة السلام عن شخص يعترف له بالتقدم في علم
الشرع فلا بد من تعرف الشرع في الوقائع منه لينوب ذلك عن
الاجتهاد والثاني أن يسعى لتحصيل العلم وحيازة رتبة الاستقلال بعلوم
الشرع فإن الإمامة وان  كانت صحيحة منعقدة في الحال فخطاب الله تعالى قائم
بايجاب العلم وافتراض تحصيله وإذا ساعدت القدرة عليه لم يكن للتواني فيه
عذر لا سيما والسن سن التحصيل وريعان الشباب معين على الغرض والقدر الواجب
تحصيله شرعا إذا صرف إليه الهمة الشريفة حصل في قدر يسير من الزمان ولا
يليق تطلب غايات الكمال إلا بالحضرة المقدسة الشريفة النبوية المحقوقة
بالعز والجلال
وإذا اتضح في هذا الباب بهذه البراهين اللائحة أن مقتضى أمر الله أن
الإمام الحق المستظهر بالله هو المتعين لخلافة الله فما أجدر هذه النعمة أن
تقابل بالشكر وإنما الشكر بالعلم وبالعمل وبالمواظبة على ما أودعته في
الباب الآخر من الكتاب وعلى الجملة فشكر هذه النعمة ألا يرضي أمير المؤمنين
أن يكون لله على وجه الأرض عبد أعبد وأشكر منه كما أن الله تعالى لم يرض أن
يكون له على وجه الأرض عبد أعز واكرم من أمير المؤمنين فهذا هو الشكر
الموازي لهذه النعمة والله ولي التوفيق نمنه ولطفه
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ق-د (ʿ-q-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Binding, knotting, compacting; a covenant firmly tied
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The contractual establishment of authority (al-ʿaqd) as a binding legal act
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical tying; metaphorical for the solemn pact of allegiance (bayʿah)
- Root: ج-ه-د (j-h-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Exertion of utmost effort; striving to one's capacity
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Independent juristic reasoning (ijtihād) as the maximal intellectual striving in deriving divine rulings
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal physical toil; metaphorical for intellectual exertion in legal inference
- Root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Superiority, excess, preeminence in merit
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The virtuous excellence (al-fāḍil) entitling one to precedence in religious office
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal surplus; metaphorical for moral and intellectual distinction
- Root: ش-و-ك (sh-w-k)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Thorns; piercing strength
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Temporal power and coercive might (shawkah) as the practical pillar of authority
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal thorns of a plant; metaphorical for formidable military and political force
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Protasis-Apodosis (al-sharṭ wa-l-jawāb) — The repeated hypothetical constructions (law... la-kāna / idhā... wajaba) govern the logical sequence of legal reasoning, each condition precisely paired with its consequent ruling.
chapters.translation:
I say: If one were to say, "The scholars have agreed in their opinions that the imamate is not contracted except for one who has attained the rank of independent juristic reasoning (ijtihād) and legal verdict-giving (fatwā) in the religious sciences, and you cannot claim the existence of this condition; and if you were to claim that this is not required, that would be a secession from the consensus of the scholars entirely — so what is your view regarding this attribute?"

We reply: If someone were to hold that attaining the degree of ijtihād is not a condition for the imamate, his statement would contain nothing but a departure from the earlier scholars — for apart from that, there is nothing in it contrary to what the evidence requires and the course of sound consideration dictates. For the conditions claimed for the imamate as a matter of Sacred Law (sharʿan) necessarily require a proof indicating them; and the proof is either an explicit text (naṣṣ) from the Lawgiver, or consideration of the public interest (maṣlaḥah) for the sake of which the imamate was sought. No explicit text has come down regarding the conditions of the imamate except concerning lineage, for he (peace be upon him) said: «الأئمة من قريش» ("The imams are from Quraysh"). As for what is beyond that, it is derived only from necessity and pressing need in the purpose of the imamate. Thus we have stipulated reason, freedom, soundness of the senses, right guidance, valor, and piety — for if these things were supposed absent, the affair of the imamate could not be ordered in any state whatsoever. But the rank of ijtihād is not something indispensable to the imamate by necessity; rather, piety that impels one to refer to the people of knowledge suffices in its place. For if the purpose is to arrange the imamate in accordance with the Sacred Law, what difference is there between one who knows the ruling of the Law through his own independent reasoning and one who knows it by following the most excellent of the people of his time? And since it is permissible for the mujtahid to rely upon the statement of a single authority — a hadith being narrated to him and he ruling by it, whether he be an imam or a judge — what then prevents him from ruling by what the scholars have agreed upon in every case, and if they differ, then following in it the statement of the most excellent and most learned? And why should he not be completed in the purpose of knowledge by the most excellent of the people of the age, just as he is completed in the purpose of might by the strongest of the people of the age, and in the purpose of sufficiency by the most astute of the people of the age and the most capable of them in opinion and discernment? Thus his dominion would never cease to be encompassed by a king among kings who strengthens him with his might, and a capable one among the capable of the age who undertakes his vizierate and aids him with his opinion and guidance, and a scholar preeminent in the sciences who conveys to his presence whatever appears of the cases of the Law in every occurrence. If someone were to say this, it would be drawn from the decisive proofs and demonstrations that are permissible to employ in matters of certainty and conviction — how much more so in matters of conjecture and estimation? For most of the questions of the imamate and its rulings are jurisprudential (fiqhiyyah) matters of probability, ruled upon in accordance with the preponderant opinion. And what I have mentioned is a clear path therein. However, I do not prefer departure from the earlier scholars, nor deviation from the highway of the departed imams — for singularness in opinion and secession from the agreement of the masses is not free from stirring aversion in hearts. But I shall seek a path borrowed from the words of the aforementioned imams, and say:

The people have differed as to whether, if the people of choice (ahl al-ikhtiyār) were to contract the pledge of allegiance (bayʿah) for the inferior (al-mafḍūl) and turn away from the superior (al-afḍal), the imamate would be contracted — despite their agreement that advancing the superior when one is able is obligatory and determined. Then the majority held that if it is contracted for the inferior while the superior is present, it is contracted, and it is not permissible to depose him on account of the superior. From this point I shall construct my argument and say: If we were to return the matter at the inception of appointment between a mujtahid in the religious sciences and one deficient therein, then advancing the mujtahid would be determined — for following one's own knowledge through independent reasoning has a superiority of rank over following another's knowledge through emulation (taqlīd). And superior merits are not to be neglected when one is able to observe them. But if the imamate has been contracted by the pledge of allegiance or by the appointment of a successor (wilāyat al-ʿahd) for one devoid of the rank of ijtihād, and might (shawkah) has arisen for him, and necks have submitted to him, and hearts have inclined toward him — then if the age is devoid of a Qurashī mujtahid combining all the conditions, it is obligatory to continue upon the contracted imamate, provided might has arisen for him. And this is the ruling of our age.

And if one were to suppose, by way of example, the presence of a Qurashī mujtahid combining piety, sufficiency, and all the conditions of the imamate, and the Muslims' need to depose the first would entail exposing themselves to stirring seditions (fitan) and the disruption of affairs — it would not be permissible for them to depose him and replace him with the other. Rather, obedience to him is obligatory upon them, and the ruling is the effectiveness of his authority and the validity of his imamate. For we know that knowledge is a merit observed in the imamate to improve the matter and to attain the additional interest in independence of judgment and freedom from emulation; and that the fruit sought from the imamate is the extinguishing of seditions that blaze in the divergence of conflicting opinions. So how could a rational person deem it permissible to stir sedition, disturb the order of affairs, and forfeit the very interest of the present state, in aspiration toward a subtle additional merit in the distinction between independent reasoning and emulation?

At this point, one ought to measure what befalls the creation by reason of the imam's turning from independent reasoning to the emulation of the imams, against what would befall them if they were to attempt his deposition and replacement, or rule his imamate as not contracted. And when one properly presents this discourse, one knows that the disparity between following the Sacred Law through independent reasoning and following it through emulation is near and slight, and that it is not permissible that the foundations of the imamate be breached on its account.

And this is an estimation in which we have been lenient in two respects: first, the supposition of a Qurashī mujtahid combining all the attributes, presenting himself for the office of the imamate — and this has no existence in our age; and second, the supposition of the creation's power to replace the imam and to dispose of him by deposition and transition — and this is impossible in our time. For if all the people of the age were to unite and conspire to turn faces and hearts away from the sacred presence of al-Mustaẓhirī (may God exalt it), they would find no way to it. Thus it is incumbent upon all the scholars of the age to issue the legal verdict (fatwā) upon the validity of this imamate and its contraction by the Sacred Law.

But after this, there are two conditions: First, that no problematic case be decided except after eliciting the insights of the scholars and seeking their support; and that one choose for his emulation, when the matter is obscure and opinions differ, the most excellent of the people of the age and the most abundant of them in knowledge. And rarely is the City of Peace (Madīnat al-Salām) devoid of a person acknowledged for preeminence in the religious science — so it is necessary to learn the Sacred Law in occurrences from him, so that this may stand in place of ijtihād.

Second, that one strive to acquire knowledge and attain the rank of independence in the religious sciences. For even if the imamate is valid and contracted in the present state, the address of God (exalted be He) stands firm in obligating knowledge and making its acquisition incumbent. And when ability assists one in it, there is no excuse for negligence therein — especially when the age is the age of acquisition and the prime of youth assists in the purpose. And the measure obligatory to acquire by the Sacred Law, if the noble resolve is directed to it, is obtained in a small measure of time. And the pursuit of the ultimate ends of perfection befits none but the sacred, noble, prophetic presence, deserving of might and majesty.

And when it has become clear in this chapter, through these shining proofs, that the requirement of God's command is that the true imam — al-Mustaẓhir bi-Allāh (he who seeks victory through God) — is the one determined for the vicegerency of God, then how fitting is this blessing to be met with gratitude! And gratitude is only through knowledge, through action, and through persistence upon what I have deposited in the other chapter of the book. And in sum, the gratitude for this blessing is that the Commander of the Faithful not be pleased that there be upon the face of the earth a servant more worshipful and more grateful to God than himself — just as God (exalted be He) was not pleased that there be upon the face of the earth a servant more mighty and more honored than the Commander of the Faithful. This then is the gratitude commensurate with this blessing. And God is the Guardian of success; we seek it from His grace and kindness.

chapters.title_en: Section 31 — The Tenth Chapter on the Religious Duties by whose Perpetual Observance the Entitlement to the Imamate Endures
chapters.arabic_text: ### | الباب العاشر في الوظائف الدينية التي بالمواظبة عليها يدوم استحقاق الإمامة ومن فرائض الدين على امير المؤمنين زاده الله توفيقا المداومة على مطالعة هذا الباب والاستقصاء على تأمله وتصفحه ومطالبة النفس الكريمة حتى تستمر عليه فإن ساعد التوفيق للمجاهدة في
chapters.anchors:
- Root: و-ظ-ف (wa-ẓa-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Assignment of a recurring task or fixed obligation; a stipulated charge (waẓīfah) that binds one to regular performance.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Religious duties (al-waẓāʾif al-dīniyyah) as divinely ordained recurrent acts that sustain the moral and spiritual order of the community.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of a fixed apportioned task; here used metaphorically for the perpetual devotional obligations incumbent upon the Imam.
- Root: د-و-م (d-w-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Continuity, permanence, and unbroken persistence in an act or state.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Steadfastness (al-mudāwamah) as the condition for the enduring validity of one's entitlement (istiḥqāq).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: uninterrupted duration; metaphorical: the moral constancy required for leadership.
- Root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Possession, dominion, and rightful claim.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Entitlement (istiḥqāq) as a juridico-theological status conferred by sustained obedience.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: ownership; metaphorical: the deserving of authority through continuous merit.
- Root: ج-ه-د (j-h-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Exertion of effort, striving against difficulty.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Spiritual struggle (mujāhadah) against the lower self as a prerequisite for divine assistance (tawfīq).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: physical exertion; metaphorical: the inner combat of the soul in devotional discipline.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Continuity (al-sharṭ wa-al-jazāʾ) — The clause "فإن ساعد التوفيق" (if divine success aids) functions as a protasis whose apodosis is implied in the preceding exhortation, indicating that the permanence of the Imamate is contingent upon sustained devotional practice.
chapters.translation: I say: The Tenth Chapter, concerning the religious duties by whose perpetual observance the entitlement to the Imamate endures. Among the obligations of the faith upon the Commander of the Faithful — may God increase him in success — is the constant application to the study of this chapter, the thoroughness in pondering and examining it, and the summoning of the noble soul until it perseveres therein. For if divine success aids in the striving (mujāhadah) [against the lower self], then [the entitlement endures].

chapters.title_en: The Attainment of Supreme Felicity Through the Four Foundational Sciences and the Duties of the Caliphate
chapters.arabic_text:
الاقتدار على وظيفة من هذه الوظائف ولو في سنة فهي السعادة القصوى وهذه
الوظائف بعضها علمية وبعضها عملية فتقدم العلمية فإن العلم هو الأصل والعمل
فرع له إذ العلوم لا حصر لها ولكنا نذكر اربعة أمورهن أمهات وأصول
الأول أن يعرف أن الإنسان في هذا العالم لم خلق وإلى أي مقصد وجه ولأي
مطلب رشح وليس يخفى على ذي بصيرة أن هذه الدار ليست دار مقر وإنما هي دار
ممر والناس فيها على صورة المسافرين ومبدأ سفرهم بطون أمهاتهم والدار
الآخرة مقصد سفرهم وزمان الحياة مقدار المسافة وسنوه منازله وشهوره فراسخه
وأيامه أمياله وأنفاسه خطاه ويصار بهم عبر السفينة براكبها ولكل شخص عند
الله عمر مقدر لا يزيد ولا ينقص ولهذا  قال عيسى صلوات الله عليه وسلم
الدنيا قنطرة فاعبروها ولا تعمروها وقد دعى الخلق الى لقاء الله في دار
السلام وسعادة الأبد فقال الله تعالى {والله يدعو إلى دار السلام} وهذا
السفر لا يفضى إلى المقصد إلا بزاد وهو التقوى ولذلك قال تعالى
{وتزودوا فإن خير الزاد التقوى} فمن لم يتزود في دنياه لآخرته بالمواظبة
على العبادة فسيرجع منه عند الموت ما اغتر من جسده وماله فيتحسر حيث لا
يغنيه التحسر ويقول {يا ليتنا نرد ولا نكذب بآيات ربنا ونكون من المؤمنين}
ويقول {فهل لنا من شفعاء فيشفعوا لنا أو نرد فنعمل غير الذي كنا نعمل}
فحينئذ {لا ينفع نفسا إيمانها لم تكن آمنت من قبل أو كسبت في إيمانها خيرا}
وهذا الإنسان من وجه آخرفي دنياه حارث وعمله حرثه ودنياه محترثه ووقت الموت
وقت حصاده ولذلك قال صلى الله عليه وسلم الدنيا مزوعة الآخرة وانما البذر
هو العمر فمن انقضى عليه نفس من انفاسه ولم يعبد الله فيه بطاعة فهو مغبون
لضياع ذلك النفس فإنه لا يعود قط ومثال الإنسان في عمره مثال رجل كان يبيع
الثلج وقت الصيف ولم تكن له بضاعة سواه فكان ينادي ويقول ارحموا من رأس
ماله يذوب فرأس مال الإنسان عمره الذي هو وقت طاعته وانه ليذوب على الدوام
فكلما زاد سنه نقص بقية عمره فزيادته نقصانه على التحقيق ومن لم ينتهز في
انفاسه حتى يقتنص بها الطاعات كلها كان مغبونا ولذلك قال صلى الله عليه
وسلم من استوى يوماه فهو مغبون ومن كان يومه شرا من أمسه فهو ملعون فكل من
صرف عمره إلى ديناه فقد خاب سعيه وضاع عمله كما قال تعالى {من كان يريد
الحياة الدنيا وزينتها نوف إليهم أعمالهم} الآية ومن عمل لآخرته فهو الذي
أنجح سعيه كما قال تعالى {ومن أراد الآخرة وسعى لها سعيها وهو مؤمن فأولئك
كان سعيهم مشكورا}
الوظيفة الثانية أنه مهما عرف أن زاد السفر إلى الآخرة التقوى فليعلم أن
التقوى محلها ومنبعها القلب لقوله  صلى الله عليه وسلم التقوى
ها هنا وأشار إلى صدره وينبغي أن يكون الاجتهاد في إصلاح القلب أولا إذ
صلاح الجوارح تابع له لقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن في بدن ابن آدم لبضعة
إذا صلحت صلح لها سائر الجسد وإذا فسدت فسد لها سائر الجسد ألا وهي القلب
وإصلاح القلب شرطه تقدم تطهيره عليه وطهارته في أن يطهر عن حب الدنيا لقوله
صلى الله عليه وسلم حب الدنيا رأس كل خطيئة وهذا هو الداء الذي أعجز الخلق
ومن ظن أنه يقدر على الجمع بين التنعم في الدنيا والحرص على ترتيب أسبابها
وبين سعادة الآخرة فهو مغرور كمن يطمع في الجمع بين الماء والنار لقوله
أمير المؤمنين رضى الله عنه الدنيا والآخرة ضرتان مهما أرضيت إحداهما أسخطت
الأخرى نعم لو كان الإنسان يشتغل بالدنيا لأجل الدين لا لأجل شهوته كمن
يصرف عمره إلى تدبير مصالح الخلق شفقة عليهم أو يصرف بعض أوقاته إلى كسب
القوت ونيته في كسب القوت إلى أن يتقوى بتناوله على الطاعة والتقوى فهذا من
عين الدين وعلى هذا المنهاج جرى حرص الأنبياء والخلفاء الراشدين في أمور
الدنيا ومهما ثبت أن الزاد هو التقوى وأن التقوى شرطها خلو القلب عن حب
الدنيا فليكن الجهد في تخليته عن حبها وطريقه أن يعرف الإنسان عيب الدنيا
وآفتها ويعرف شرف السعادة في الدار الآخرة وزينتها ويعلم أن في مراعاة
الدنيا الحقيرة فوت الآخرة الخطيرة وأقل آفات الدنيا وهي مستيقنة لكل عاقل
وجاهل أنها منقضية على القرب وسعادة الآخرة لا آخر لها هذا إذا سلمت الدنيا
صافية عن الشوائب والأقذاء خالية عن المؤذيات والمكدرات وهيهات هيهات فلم
يسلم أحد في الدنيا من طول الأذى ومقاساة الشدائد ومهما عرف تصرم الدنيا
وتأبد السعادة في العقبى فليتأمل أنه لو شغف إنسان بشخص واستهتر به وصار لا
يطبق فراقه وخير بين أن يعجل لقاءه
ليلة واحدة بين أن يصبر عنه تلك الليلة مجاهدا نفسه ثم يخلى بينه وبينه
ألف ليلة فكيف لا يسهل عليه  الصبر ليلة واحدة لتوقع التلذذ بمشاهدته ألف
ليلة ولو استعجل تلك الليلة وعرض نفسه لعناء المفارقة ألف ليلة لعد سفيها
خارجا عن حزب العقلاء فالدنيا معشوقة كلفنا الصبر عنها مدة يسيرة ووعدنا
أضعاف هذه اللذات مدة لا آخر لها وترك الألف بالواحد ليس من العقل واختيار
الألف على الواحد المعجل ليس بمتعذر على العاقل وعند هذا ينبغي أن يقيس
الانسان أقصى مدة مقامه في الدنيا وهى مائة سنة مثلا ومدة مقامه في الاخرة
ولا آخر لها بل لو طلبنا مثالا لطول مدة الأبد لعجزنا عنه إلا أن نقول لو
قدرنا الدنيا كلها إلى منتهى السموات ممتلئة بالذرة وقدرنا طائرا يأخذ
بمنقاره في كل ألف سنة حبة واحدة فلا يزال يعود حتى لا يبقى من الذرة حبة
واحدة فتنقضي هذه المدة وقد بقى من الذرة اضعافها فكيف لا يقدر العاقل إذا
حقق على نفسه هذا الامر على أن يستحقر الدنيا ويتجرد لله تعالى هذا لو قد
قدر بقاء العمر مائة سنة وقدرت الدنيا صافية عن الاقذاء فكيف والموت
بالمرصاد في كل لحظة والدنيا غير صافية من ضروب التعب والعناء وهذا امر
ينبغي أن يطول التامل فيه حتى يترسخ في القلب ومنه تنبعث التقوى وما لم
يظهر للانسان حقارة الدنيا لا يتصور منه أن يسعى للدار الاخرى وينبغي أن
يستعان على معرفة ذلك بالاعتبار بمن سلف من أبناء الدنيا كيف تعبوا فيها ثم
ارتحلوا عنها بغير طائل ولم تصحبهم إلا الحسرة والندامة ولقد صدق من قال من
الشعراء حيث قال أشد الغم عندي في سرور تيقن عنه صاحبه انتقالا وهذه حال
لذات الدنيا
الوظيفة الثالثة أن معنى خلافة الله على الخلق اصلاح الخلق ولن يقدر على
اصلاح اهل الدنيا من لا يقدر على اصلاح اهل بلده ولن يقدر على اصلاح اهل
البلد من لايقدر على اصلاح اهل منزله ولا يقدر على اصلاح اهل منزله من
لايقدر على اصلاح نفسه ومن لا
يقدر على اصلاح نفسه فينبغي أن تقع البداية باصلاح القلب وسياسة  النفس
ومن لم يصلح نفسه وطمع في اصلاح غيره كان مغرور كما قال الله تعالى
{أتأمرون الناس بالبر وتنسون أنفسكم} وفي الحديث ان الله تعالى قال لعيسى
بن مريم عظ نفسك فان اتعظت فعظ الناس والا فاستحي مني ومثال من عجز عن
اصلاح نفسه وطمع في اصلاح غيره مثال الاعمى اذا اراد يهدي العميان وذلك لا
يستتب له قط وانما يقدر على اصلاح النفس بمعرفة النفس ومثل معرفة الانسان
في بدنه كمثل وال في بلده وجوارحه وحواسه واطرافه بمنزلة صناع وعملة والشرع
له كمشير ناصح ووزير مدبر والشهوة فيه كعبد سوء جالب للميرة والطعام والعصب
له كصاحب شرطة والعبد الجالب للميرة خبيث ماكر يتمثل للانسان بصورة الناصح
وفي نصحة دبيب العقرب فهو يعارض الوزير في تدبيره ولا يغفل ساعة من منازعته
ومعارضته فكان الوالى في مملكته متى استشار في تدبيراته وزيره دون هذا
العبد السوء الخبيث وادب صاحب شرطته وجعله مؤتمرا لوزيره وسلطه على هذا
العبد الخبيث واتباعه حتى يكون هذا العبد مسوسا لا سائسا ومدبرا لا مدبرا
استقام امر بلده وكذا النفس متى استعانت في تدبيراتها بالشرع والعقل وادبت
الحمية والغضب حتى لا يهتاج الا باشارة الشرع والعقل وسلطته على الشهوة
واستتب أمرها والا فسدت واتبعت الهوى ولذات الدنيا كما قال الله تعالى {ولا
تتبع الهوى} الأية وقال تعالى {أفرأيت من اتخذ إلهه هواه} {وقال} {أخلد إلى
الأرض واتبع هواه فمثله كمثل الكلب} وقال تعالى في مدح من عصاها {وأما من
خاف مقام ربه ونهى النفس عن الهوى}
الأية وعلى الجملة فينبغي ان يكون العبد طول عمره في مجاهدة غضبه وشهوته
ومتشمرا لمخالفتها كما يتشمر لمخالفة اعدائه فانهما عدوان كما قال صلى الله
عليه وسلم اعدى عدو نفسك التي بين جنبيك ومثال من اشتغل بالتلذذ عندالشهوات
والانتقام عند الغضب مثل رجل فارس صياد له فرس وكلب غفل عن صيده واشتغل
بتعهد فرسه وطعمة كلبه وضيع فيه جميع وقته فإن شهوة الانسان كفرسه وغضبه
ككلبه فإن كان الفارس حاذقا والفرس  مروضا والكلب مؤدبا ومعلما فهو قمين
بإدراك حاجته من الصيد ومتى كان الفارس أخرق وفرسه جموحا أو حرونا وكلبه
عقورا فلا فرسه ينبعث تحته منقادا ولا كلبه يسترسل باشارته مطيعا فهو قمين
أن يعطب فضلا أن يدرك ما طلب ومهما جاهد الإنسان فيها هواه فله ثلاثة أحوال
الأول أن يغلبه الهوى فيتبعه ويعرض عن الشرع كما قال تعالى {أفرأيت من اتخذ
إلهه هواه} الثاني أن يغالبه فيقهره مرة ويقهره الهوى أخرى فله أجر
المجاهدين وهو المرد بقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم جاهدوا هواكم كما تجاهدو
أعداءكم الثالث أن يغلب هواه ككثير من الأنبياء وصفوه الأولياء لقوله صلى
الله عليه وسلم ما من أحد إلا وله شيطان وإن الله قد أعانني على شيطاني حتى
ملكته وعلى الجملة فالشيطان يتسلط على الإنسان بحسب وجوده الهوى فيه وإنما
مثلت الشهوة بالفرس والغضب بالكلب لأنه لولاهما لما تصورت العبادة المؤدية
إلى السعادة الآخرة فإن الإنسان يحتاج في عبادته إلى بدنه ولا قيام إلا
بالقوت ولا يقدر على الاقتيات إلا بشهوة وهو محتاج إلى أن يحرس نفسه عن
الهلكات بدفعها ولا يدفع المؤذى إلا بداعية الغضب فكأنهما خادمان لبقاء
البدن والبدن مركب النفس وبواسطتها يصل إلى العبادة والعبادة طريقه إلى
النجاة
الوظيفة الرابعة أن يعرف أن الإنسان مركب من صفات ملكية
وصفات بهيمية فهو حيران بين الملك والبهيمة فمشابهته للملك بالعلم
والعبادة والعفة والعدالة والصفات المحمودة ومشابهته للبهائم بالشهوة
والغضب والحقد والصفات المذمومة فمن صرف همته إلى العلم والعمل والعبادة
فخليق أن يلحق بالملائكة فيسمى ملكا وربانيا كما قال تعالى {إن هذا إلا ملك
كريم} ومن صرف همته إلى إتباع الشهوات واللذات البدنية يأكل كما تأكل
البهائم فخليق أن يلحق بالبهائم فيصير إما غمرا كثور وإما شرها كخنزير وإما
ضرعا ككلب أو حقودا كجمل أو متكبرا كنمر أو ذا روغان ونفاق كثعلب أو يجمع
ذلك فيصير كشيطان مريد وعلى ذلك دل قوله تعالى {وجعل منهم القردة والخنازير
وعبد الطاغوت} {وقال} {كالأنعام بل هم أضل} {وقال}  {إن شر الدواب عند الله
الصم البكم الذين لا يعقلون} وهذه الصفات الذميمة تجتمع في الآدمي في هذا
العالم وهو في صورة الإنسان فتكون الصفة باطنة والصورة ظاهرة وفي الآخرة
تتحد الصورة والصفات فيصور كل شخص بصفته التي كانت غالبة عليه في حياته فمن
غلب عليه الشر حشر في صورة خنزير ومن غلب عليه الغضب حشر في صورة سبع ومن
غلب عليه الحمق حشر في صورة حمار ومن غلب عليه التكبر حشر بصورة نمر وهكذا
جميع الصفات ومن غلب عليه العلم والعمل واستولى بهما على هذه الصفات حشر في
صورة الملائكة والصديقين والشهداء والصالحين وحسن أولئك رفيقا
وهذه الوظائف التي ذكرناها علمية يجب التأمل فيها حتى تتمثل في القلب
فتكون نصب العين في كل لحظة وإنما تترسخ هذه العلوم في النفس إذا أكدت
بالعمل كما سنذكره في الوظائف العملية بعد القول في الوظائف العملية
وهي كثيرة أولاها وهي من الأمور الكلية أن كل من تولى عملا على المسلمين
فينبغي أن يحكم نفسه في كل قضية يبرمها فما لا يرتضيه لنفسه لا يرتضيه
لغيره فالمؤمنون كنفس واحدة فقد روى عبد الله بن عمر رضى الله عنهما أن
رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال من سره أن يزحزح عن النار ويدخل الجنة
فليدركه موته وهو مؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر وليأت إلى الناس الذي يحب أن
يؤتى إليه وروى أنس بن مالك عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال من
أصبح وهمه غير الله تعالى فليس من الله في شيء ومن أصبح لا يهتم بالمسلمين
فليس من المسلمين
ومنها أن يكون والى الأمر متعطشا إلى نصيحة العلماء ومتبجحا بها إذا
سمعها وشاكرا عليها فقد روى أن أبا عبيدة ومعاذا كتبا إلى عمر رضى الله
عنهم أما بعد فإنا عهدناك وشأن نفسك لك مهم وأصبحت وقد وليت بأمر هذه الأمة
أسودها وأحمرها يجلس بين يديك الشريف والوضيع والصديق والعدو ولكل حصته من
العدل فانظر كيف أنت عند ذلك يا عمر وانا  نحذرك مما حذرت الأمم قبلك يوم
تعنو فيه الوجوه وتجب فيه القلوب وتقطع فيه الحجة لعز ملك قهرهم جبروته
والخلق داخرون له ينتظرون قضاءه ويخافون عقابه وانه ذكر لنا أنه سياتي على
الناس زمان يكون اخوان العلانية أعداء السريرة فانا نعوذ بالله ان ينزل
كتابنا من قبلك سوى المنزل الذى نزل من قلوبنا وإنا كتبنا اليك نصيحة
والسلام فكاتبهما بجوابه وذكر في آخر ما كتب إنكما كتبتما الى نصيحة
فتعهداني منكما بكتاب فإني لا غنى بي عنكما والسلام عليكما
ومنها ألا يستحقر الوالى انتظار ارباب الحاجات ووقوفهم بالباب في لحظة
واحدة فان الاهتمام بأمر المسلمين أهم له وأعود عليه مما هو متشاغل به من
نوافل العبادات فضلا عن اتباع الشهوات فقد روى أن عمر بن عبد العزيز رضى
الله عنه جلس يوما للناس فلما انتصف النهار ضجر ومل فقال للناس مكانكم حتى
أعود اليكم فدخل يستريح ساعة فجاء ابنه عبد الملك فاستأذن فدخل عليه فقال
يا أمير المؤمنين ما سبب دخولك قال أردت ان استريح ساعة فقال أأمنت أن
يأتيك الموت ورعيتك على الباب ينتظرونك وانت محتجب عنهم فقال عمر صدقت فقام
من ساعته وخرج الى الناس
ومنها أن يترك الوالي للأمر الترفه والتلذذ بالشهوات في المأكولات
والملبوسات فقد روى أن عمر رضى الله عنه كتب الى سلمان الفارسي يستزيره
فلما قدم عليه سلمان تلقاه في أصحابه فالتزمه وضمه إليه وصار الى المدينة
فلما خلا به عمر قال له يا أخي هل بلغك مني ما تكرهه فقال لا قال عزمت عليك
إن كان بلغك مني ما تكرهه ألا أخبرتني فقال لولا ما عزمت على أولا ما
أخبرتك بلغني أنك تجمع بين السمن واللحم على مائدتك وبلغني أن لك حلتين حلة
تلبسها مع أهلك وحلة تخرج فيها إلى الناس فقال عمر هل بلغك غير هذا فقال لا
فقال أما هذان فقد كفيتهما فلا أعود إليهما ومنها أن يعلم والى الأمر أن
العبادة تيسر للولاة مالا يتيسر لآحاد الرعايا فلتغتنم الولاية لتعبد  الله
بها وذلك بالتواضع والعدل والنصح للمسلمين والشفقة عليهم فقد روى عن أبي
بكر رضى الله عنه وهو على المنبر قال سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
يقول الوالي العدل المتواضع ظل الله ورمحه في أرضه فمن نصحه في نفسه وفي
عباد الله حشره الله تعالى في وقده يوم لا ظل إلا ظله وفي غشه في نفسه وفي
عباد الله خذله الله تعالى يوم القيامة ويرفع للوالي العدل
المتواضع في كل يوم وليلة عمل ستين صديقا كلهم عبد مجتهد في نفسه فهذه
رتبة عظيمة لا تسلم في كل عصر إلا لواحد وانما تنال هذه الرتبة بالعدل
والتواضع وقد روى أبو سعيد الخدرى عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال
سبعة يظلهم الله يوم القيامة يوم لا ظل إلا ظله إمام عادل وشاب نشأ في
عبادة الله ورجل قلبه متعلق بالمسجد إذا خرج من حتى يعود إليه ورجلان تحابا
في الله فاجتمعا على ذلك وتفرقا عليه ورجل ذكر الله خاليا ففاضت عيناه ورجل
دعته امرأة ذات حسب وجمال إلى نفسها فقال أني أخاف الله رب العالمين ورجل
تصدق بصدقة وأخفاها حتى لا تعلم شماله ما تنفق يمينه فهذه سبع لا يتصور
اجتماعها إلا في أمير المؤمنين وإنما يقدر غيره من الخلق على آحادها دون
مجموعها فليجتهد في نيل رتبة لم تدخر إلا له ولن يقوم بها سواه فقد روى
ايضا أبو سعيد الخدرى أنه قال إن أحب العباد إلى الله تعالى وأقربهم منه
مجلسا إمام عادل وإن أبغض الناس إلى الله وأشدهم عذابا يوم القيامة إمام
جائر وقد روى أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال ثلاثة لا يرد الله
